purpose.question: Do the frozen SQG twins satisfy the ordered conditions under which a two-field closure reduces to the scalar logistic law: (D1) one shape, Delta(k,t) = a(t)U(k); (D2) one clock, G(k)/U(k) independent of k; controlled residuals; and only then (D3) coefficient identification, lambdabar = lambda_TL?
purpose.question_provenance: these are divergences 1, 2 and 5 of THEORY_closure_comparison_2026-08-09.tex. Divergence 3 (memory D dependent on a) is not measurable from twin fields. Divergence 4 (finite-band leakage) belongs to M3A and is out of scope here.
purpose.original_r1_question_retained: Do the twins realize Delta(k,t) = a(t)U(k), or a moving similarity spectrum Delta/U = r(k/k_e(t))? This remains the D1 question and is answered by R, b, k_half and Q.
purpose.explicit_non_claim: M-Tb is not a held-out predictive test and contains no relational null. It cannot produce, support, or modify an E-axis verdict (E0-E3), and it cannot modify C0. Its outputs are measured magnitudes for the residuals that M-T is required to quantify.
purpose.decision_relevance: The T1 gate is conjunctive and ordered. D1 must return ONE_SHAPE_LIMIT, D2 must return ONE_CLOCK, the relevant residuals must be controlled, and only then is D3 interpretable as a comparison of the GT1 kernel coefficient with lambda_TL. D3 alone cannot resolve the T-code in either direction. If D1 or D2 selects MOVING_FRONT or MANY_CLOCKS, the lifecycle logistic fit is not script-G/E and D3 has no theorem meaning; M-T owes GT2 or another corrected law. T2 is entered only after that alternative law or coefficient relation is derived. Without a completed alternative, the charter result is T0, not T3.
purpose.relation_to_M_T: Delivered at or before the M-T midpoint checkpoint. Informs where M-T spends cap; does not license any T-verdict, which requires the §3.1 proof standard independently.

anti_ratchet_clause.statement: No outcome of M-Tb may reduce a claim. Every tier in item 4 routes to a DERIVATION OBLIGATION on M-T, not to a verdict. M-Tb selects WHICH scalar law M-T must derive; it never concludes that no law exists.
anti_ratchet_clause.rationale: Across eight prior iterations the adjustment variable was always the claim and never the theory. A measured failure of the one-shape ansatz N1 is not the absence of a scalarization: the Leith-Kraichnan moving similarity form Delta/U = r(k/k_e(t)) is itself a one-parameter family, with front position k_e(t) replacing amplitude a(t), and therefore also closes to a scalar law. Which law is an open derivation, not a demotion.
anti_ratchet_clause.reconciliation_hypothesis: N1 is the broad-front limit of the similarity picture. When the front width in log k exceeds the band width, all shells decorrelate together, a(k,t) -> a(t), and the moving-front law reduces to logistic. The reconciling parameter is the measurable ratio W_front / W_band, which M-Tb reports (item 2, front_width).
forbidden_conclusions: 'N1 fails, therefore the scalar law is not derivable' — this is T3 by assertion and is prohibited; T3 requires showing NO scalar reduction exists for the measured geometry
'N1 fails, therefore C0 weakens' — M-Tb cannot modify C0 under any outcome
any statement that treats a measured spectral geometry as a negative result rather than as the input to a derivation

lifecycle_interval.rule: field times at which the band-mean rho on k10_20 lies in [0.15, 0.85]
lifecycle_interval.cadence: field cadence 0.1 TU over 0-12 TU (125 stored field times; only 4 lie beyond t=12)
lifecycle_interval.provenance: the [0.15, 0.85] bracket is the interval already frozen and reported response-blind in M2A_FEASIBILITY_2026-08-09.json; it is inherited, not chosen here

per_shell_quantities.implementation: the M2a arbitrary-band machinery in audit_nested_band_feasibility_v1.py, applied at width-one bands; all conversions through conventions_v1.py

primary_statistic.name: R
primary_statistic.abar: U-weighted mean of a(k,t) over shells 10-20
primary_statistic.weights: w_k proportional to Et(k,t) (background/truth energy in shell)
primary_statistic.weight_justification: under N1 the conversion integrand carries U(k); U-weighting matches how a enters the conversion integral
primary_statistic.meaning: R is exactly the fractional error induced in the a(1-a) conversion coefficient by replacing scale-dependent a(k,t) with its band mean, since <a(1-a)> - abar(1-abar) = -Var_k(a). It is the ledger N3 spectral-shape residual.
primary_statistic.summary: per trajectory, the median of R(t) over the lifecycle interval; then the median over the 4 truths within a regime

secondary_statistic_moving_spectrum.name: b and k_half
secondary_statistic_moving_spectrum.b: U-weighted least-squares slope of a(k,t) against log(k) over shells 10-20
secondary_statistic_moving_spectrum.k_half: the wavenumber at which the fitted a(k,t) profile crosses 0.5, by linear interpolation in log k; censored when the crossing lies outside [10, 20]
secondary_statistic_moving_spectrum.drift: Spearman rank correlation of k_half(t) with t over the lifecycle interval
secondary_statistic_moving_spectrum.role: distinguishes the two geometries: symmetric scatter about a band-uniform amplitude versus a systematic moving similarity front

secondary_statistic_front_width.name: W_front and the reconciliation ratio
secondary_statistic_front_width.W_front: the width in log10(k) over which the fitted a(k,t) profile rises from 0.25 to 0.75, by interpolation in log k; censored when either crossing lies outside shells 10-20
secondary_statistic_front_width.role: PRIMARY INPUT TO THE DERIVATION OBLIGATION. Q is the parameter that reconciles the one-shape and moving-front pictures: Q >> 1 means the front is broad compared with the band, all shells share one amplitude, and N1 is the correct limit; Q << 1 means a sharp front traverses the band and the similarity variable k_e(t) is the correct scalar coordinate.
secondary_statistic_front_width.summary: median of Q(t) over the lifecycle interval, per trajectory, then per truth, then per regime, with truth-level bootstrap CI
secondary_statistic_front_width.censoring_note: Q is right-censored whenever the front is broader than the band, which is itself the N1-favourable outcome; censored fractions must be reported and a lower bound on Q given, never silently dropped

item_2_primary_response_predictor_and_co.comparator: the N1 ansatz itself, i.e. the degenerate profile a(k,t) = abar(t), for which R = 0 and b = 0 identically

D2_one_clock_test.why_added: R tests only divergence 1 (spectral shape). The actual hypothesis of Theorem 1 is the pointwise eigencondition G(k)/U(k) = lambda, which is divergence 2 and which R does not test. The source document states at its 'first point of divergence' item 2 that G(k)/U(k) may vary with k even where Delta is approximately aU.
D2_one_clock_test.measurable_form: invert the pointwise reduction U(k) adot = a(1-a) G(k) to obtain lambda_eff(k,t) = adot(k,t) / ( a(k,t) * (1 - a(k,t)) ), which equals G(k)/U(k) and is therefore the eigencondition residual, measured without any closure model
D2_one_clock_test.independence_note: This is a DISPERSION question — whether lambda_eff is flat in k — not a comparison against an independently measured rate. No held-out response is used and the M2a independent-lambda_b blocker does not apply.
D2_one_clock_test.statistic: Lambda_disp(t) = U-weighted standard deviation of log(lambda_eff(k,t)) across shells 10-20; summarised as the median over the lifecycle interval, per trajectory then per truth then per regime
D2_one_clock_test.derivative_rule: adot by centred finite difference on the 0.1 TU dense field cadence, after a predeclared 3-point moving average on a(k,t); the unsmoothed variant is a predeclared sensitivity
D2_one_clock_test.endpoint_guard: lambda_eff diverges as a -> 0 or a -> 1; restrict to shells and times with a(k,t) in [0.15, 0.85], matching the existing lifecycle rule. Excluded (k,t) counts are reported.

geometry_tiers.meaning: rates agree across the band to about 10 percent; the eigencondition is numerically realised
geometry_tiers.derivation_obligation: M-T proceeds to identify the coefficient; Theorem 1's hypothesis is empirically supported in this band
M-T derives the leading correction from clock dispersion and the domain over which one clock suffices

M-T derives the scalar law for a k-dependent rate profile, or shows the reduction requires a bandwise vector rather than one scalar exposure (the source document's own language in its compact-record section). NOT an obstruction record.

D2_one_clock_test.predicted_direction: MANY_CLOCKS in n512_re940_marginal; smaller dispersion in n256_re470_steep
D2_one_clock_test.independence_from_R: R and Lambda_disp can disagree in either direction. R small with Lambda_disp large is the case the source document explicitly warns about and is the most decision-relevant outcome; it must be reported prominently if observed.

D3_coefficient_identification_test.why_added: The source document derives the logistic FORM with coefficient lambdabar = script-G / E, a closure-kernel rate. The manuscript claim uses lambda_TL. Their equality is still a ledger assumption. D3 is a necessary but not sufficient T1 diagnostic, and it is interpretable only after the D1, D2, and residual gates establish that the fitted lifecycle coefficient estimates script-G/E.
D3_coefficient_identification_test.feasibility: FEASIBLE NOW, NO PATH B. lambda_TL is stored for the frozen primary band as lambda_energy_rate band index 2 at 1200 times. No new tangent-linear integration is required.
D3_coefficient_identification_test.restricted_to: k10_20 only. Inner nested bands have no stored lambda_TL; that remains the M2a blocker and is out of scope.
D3_coefficient_identification_test.ordering_and_interpretability_gate: Evaluate D1, then D2, then residual control. Interpret D3 as a GT1 coefficient comparison only if D1 = ONE_SHAPE_LIMIT, D2 = ONE_CLOCK, and the relevant spectral, band-boundary, dissipation, and forcing residuals are controlled at the predeclared level. Otherwise D3 may be computed only as a labelled descriptive sensitivity and cannot enter a T-code.
D3_coefficient_identification_test.statistic: the ratio lambda_fit / lambda_TL, where lambda_fit is the rate fitted from the band-integrated logistic over the lifecycle interval and lambda_TL is the stored tangent-linear half-energy rate over a predeclared matched early-time window. Rename lambda_fit as lambdabar = script-G/E only after the interpretability gate passes.
D3_coefficient_identification_test.reporting: report the D1, D2, and residual gates before the ratio. If any gate fails, label the ratio NOT INTERPRETABLE FOR GT1. If all gates pass, report per trajectory with truth-level bootstrap CI; always report the ratio and CI, never only a binary tier.

tiers.consequence: necessary coefficient evidence for T1, but not sufficient: the analytical and numerical proof gates must also pass

tiers.condition: all interpretability gates pass and the CI excludes 1
tiers.consequence: routes to a T2 coefficient branch; T2 is assigned only after M-T derives the relation between the kernel and tangent-linear rates

tiers.condition: D1, D2, or residual control fails
tiers.consequence: the fitted coefficient is not script-G/E and the comparison has no T-code implication; route M-T to GT2 or the corrected-law derivation

D3_coefficient_identification_test.boundary_with_forbidden_M2: D3 compares two growth-rate summaries. It does not compute, fit, or report the closure ratio P_b / (lambda_b * epsilon_b), which remains forbidden under item 3. Before the interpretability gate passes, the lifecycle fit must be called lambda_fit, not lambdabar or script-G/E.

item_3_independent_lambda_b.justification: M-Tb is a shape test on decorrelation structure, not a rate or closure test. No infinitesimal rate enters R, b, or k_half. The M2a blocker (missing independent lambda_b for inner bands) therefore does not apply.
item_3_independent_lambda_b.prohibition: M-Tb may not compute, fit, or report any band closure ratio P_b / (lambda_b * epsilon_b). Doing so converts it into an unauthorized M2.

geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.measured_geometry: band-uniform decorrelation amplitude; the front is broad compared with the band (Q >> 1)
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.derivation_obligation: M-T derives the coefficient K under N1/N3 and reports the residual. The empirical premise of the logistic reduction is verified in this regime; the coefficient bias from scalarization is at most 5 percent.
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.verdict_this_licenses: none by itself; supports a T1 branch only if M-T meets the §3.1 proof standard including the numerical confirmation gate

geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.measured_geometry: partial scale coherence; front width comparable to band width (Q of order 1)
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.derivation_obligation: M-T derives the leading correction to the logistic coefficient in powers of R, giving logistic plus a quantified O(R) shape correction and the domain over which the correction is negligible.
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.verdict_this_licenses: none by itself; a derived correction is T1-with-domain or T2 depending on whether the corrected law remains logistic in form

geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.measured_geometry: a sharp decorrelation front traverses the band; the similarity variable k_e(t) rather than the amplitude a(t) is the correct scalar coordinate (Q < 1)
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.derivation_obligation: M-T derives the scalar law implied by the measured similarity geometry, using k_e(t) as the one-parameter family, and identifies the limit in which it reduces to logistic. It does NOT record an obstruction. The moving similarity form is a one-parameter family and therefore closes to a scalar law; which law is the open question and is precisely what the cap is for.
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.verdict_this_licenses: none by itself; the expected branch is T2 with logistic as an explicit special case. T3 is available ONLY if M-T proves that no scalar reduction exists for this measured geometry, which is a strictly higher bar than 'N1 fails'.
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.scoping_note: A sharp-front calculation on U ~ k^-n with front propagation at the local strain rate lambda(k) ~ k^((3-n)/2) yields d(eps)/dt proportional to (eps + eps_0)^p with p = -(5-3n)/(2(n-1)). This reproduces exponential growth at n=3 (p=1) and Lorenz (1969) finite-time linear growth at n=5/3 (p=0). It is recorded here as evidence that the derivation target is real and reachable, NOT as a derivation and NOT as a result. M-T owns the actual calculation, including finite-band boundary terms and the smooth-front generalisation.
geometry_tiers_on_primary_statistic_R.validity_caveat: The moving-front model presumes upscale error migration and is not expected to hold for steep spectra where lambda(k) decreases with k and error grows in place rather than propagating. The two regimes may therefore require different laws; this is a result, not a failure.

item_4_numerical_tolerances.tier_justification: The tiers are stated in units of coefficient error because R is literally the fractional conversion-coefficient error, not an arbitrary goodness score. 0.05 and 0.25 are declared before inspection.
item_4_numerical_tolerances.tier_semantics: These are GEOMETRY tiers, not verdict tiers. Each names a measured spectral geometry and the derivation M-T then owes. No tier is a negative result and no tier reduces a claim. See purpose.anti_ratchet_clause.

item_7_null_statistic_and_multiplicity.frozen_nulls_untouched: the frozen v8 verdicts p_time = 0.011, p_cross = 113/384, p_phase = 0.001 are not recomputed, reinterpreted, or referenced as support

item_9_predicted_direction.label: PROSPECTIVE_MAGNITUDE — the SIGN is not open; see sign_is_not_a_prediction

sign_is_not_a_prediction.finding: Verification against references/LeithKraichnan1972.pdf p.1049 shows LK themselves define the error ratio function r(k/k_e) = Delta(k,t)/U(k) and define k_e(t) as the wavenumber at which Delta/U = 0.5, and report that r(x) is INCREASING in x and that the similarity spectrum moves toward lower wavenumbers. P3 and P4 below are therefore LK's published findings for an inertial range, not predictions of this record.
sign_is_not_a_prediction.consequence: The statistics a(k,t), k_half and Q are LK's own standard diagnostics — which strengthens them — but item 9 must not claim prospective credit for their direction. What is genuinely open, and what this record predicts, is MAGNITUDE: how large R and Q are within a finite eleven-shell band of these SQG twins, at this Reynolds number and spectral slope.
sign_is_not_a_prediction.excluded_regime: LK p.1049 further report that while correlated and uncorrelated regions are separated by a sharp discontinuity, sweeping of uncorrelated energy to high wavenumbers overpowers conversion and THE ERROR DECREASES. A logistic law with lambda > 0 cannot produce d(eps)/dt < 0 at small eps. The rho window [0.15, 0.85] already excludes this transient; it is recorded here as a NAMED excluded regime rather than a silent crop.

item_9_predicted_direction.basis: WPT_assumption_ledger_v1.md, 'Prior literature boundary', and direct verification of Leith (1971) Eqs. (11)-(12) p.149 and Leith & Kraichnan (1972) Eqs. (2)-(5) p.1043 and Section 4 p.1049 against the scanned primary sources in references/.
predictions: P1: in n512_re940_marginal, R > 0.25 and Q < 1 (tier MOVING_FRONT), obligating M-T to derive the similarity-variable scalar law
P2: R is smaller and Q larger in n256_re470_steep than in n512_re940_marginal, because the steeper spectrum is more scale-coherent
P3: b(t) > 0 across the lifecycle interval (decorrelation increases with wavenumber)
P4: the Spearman correlation of k_half with t is negative (the decorrelation front migrates upscale), which is the moving-front signature rather than symmetric scatter
item_9_predicted_direction.what_these_predictions_are_about: P1-P4 predict WHICH SCALAR LAW M-T must derive. They are not predictions that a claim will shrink. Under the anti-ratchet clause, confirming P1 obligates the moving-front derivation (expected branch T2 with logistic as a special case); refuting P1 verifies the N1 premise empirically and obligates the coefficient derivation (expected branch T1 with domain). Both outcomes send M-T to a derivation and neither weakens C0.
item_9_predicted_direction.symmetry_note: Declaring a direction that disfavours the originally assumed geometry is required by ADVISORY_to_Sol_theory_symmetry_2026-08-09.md §3, but it is only legitimate because every tier carries a derivation obligation. A predicted-failure direction paired with a menu of verdicts would be the ratchet, not a test.
